firstFailuresAndCorrections: DB worker first interceptor assumed SET column order (18 failures); regex now recognizes the poster SET anywhere. These agent-only results are not added to main totals.

New root fixture typecheck exposed missing style guard, unsupported synthetic model IDs, sequenceUrl and a partial plan; fixed using actual registry defaults, required fields and an explicitly marked executor stub.
Client worker fixed a failed-read/trailing-signal case before integration; no independent acceptance is inferred from that report.
Independent review found warm reverted-fetch fulfillment and entirely cold clear races. Both failed before correction and pass after actual success receipts and synchronous query lifetime.
A closure-mutated primitive caused one new lint warning; a mutable read receipt preserves semantics without a rule suppression. Final lint is back to the original 147 warnings.

scope.method: Static source review of coordinator, regression sources, related launch/reconciliation and delivery paths, and installed dependency source and ESM runtime behavior.
scope.supporting_files: Manifest binds whole files; supporting files were reviewed at the relevant call paths and dependency implementations.

initial_findings.title: Warm cancellation could consume the only poster refresh signal
initial_findings.original_race: Continue cancels a warm detail fetch before registering its pending launch. Query-core can fulfill that cancelled fetch with reverted cached data. The former coordinator then closed with dirty=false, so an insufficient-credit refusal could leave the stale poster without a remaining refresh obligation.

resolution.explanation: Each read subscribes before fetchQuery to non-manual success events on the exact detail key in that QueryClient. Fulfillment without such a success sets dirty=true. The per-read subscription is removed in finally. Reverted warm data and manual setQueryData do not count as authoritative read completion, and pending launch checks retain the obligation until registry completion.
resolution.regression_review: Source inspected only; synthetic launch registry completion models refusal rather than invoking the entire Continue UI handler.

initial_findings.title: A queued empty-cache refresh could survive clear and recreate detail
initial_findings.original_race: Before the first awaited cancellation settles, neither a detail nor a launch query need exist. clear() then emitted no matching removed event, allowing the queued refresh to fetch and recreate detail after teardown.

resolution.explanation: The exact detail query is synchronously built after the lifetime watcher is installed and before startRefresh reaches its first await. Immediate clear now removes that entry, closes the coordinator, and prevents resumed reads from fetching. Building the lifetime neither writes a poster nor starts a network request.
resolution.regression_review: Source inspected only; the test clears a wholly cold client immediately after scheduling refresh.

static_checks.reasoning: Only a non-manual success on the exact detail key can fulfill the read obligation. Errors and cold cancellation retain the existing error/cancellation paths; finally removes the read-scoped listener.

Pending state is checked after both awaits. A pending launch marks dirty and cancels an active poster read. A completion notification either starts a stopped drain or is observed by the already-running drain. Poster refresh does not call finishGenerationLaunch or arm owner confirmation.
Signals received during a read set dirty=true on the shared state. Successful completion never resets that trailing dirty flag. The state remains scoped by QueryClient and sequence.

static_checks.outcome: No actionable issue found in the focused fixes
static_checks.reasoning: The cold lifetime is registered synchronously. Detail removal closes the coordinator and dependency destruction cancels its fetch. Closed states cannot restart or delete a later state; each per-read listener is removed when its fetch settles.

static_checks.check: Payload, lifecycle and other event semantics
static_checks.reasoning: Poster URL payloads are not installed in cache. Owned and legacy posters remain refresh signals, with no lifecycle action or lifecycle-owner adoption. Existing terminal guards and non-poster dispatch rules are unchanged.

validation.fixed_suite: Primary executor reports 61 tests across four files and 535 tests across 28 files, plus typecheck/build passing before the receipt-only lint correction. Final lint/typecheck/tests/build are managed by the primary executor; the reviewer did not execute or independently verify those checks. No end-user testing or acceptance is asserted.
